title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the notes describe the complex-analytic uniformization of the moduli of elliptic curves M_{1,1}^{an}. A 'structure de Torelli' on E is an isomorphism u : Z^2 -> Pi. Here Pi is the period lattice H_1(E,Z), viewed inside the complex line t_E (the tangent space / Lie algebra of E). Equivalently it is a framing of H_1, i.e. a Teichmüller-type rigidification. With z1 = u(e1) and z2 = u(e2), the previous page set up the correspondence (24): the point of the half-plane D attached to u is z = -conj(z2/z1). It is not the naive tau = z2/z1. This comes from Grothendieck's way of identifying complex structures on R^2 with points of D.

On this page he computes how the right action u -> u∘g of g = (a b; c d) in SL(2,Z) moves z.
- The new basis is z'1 = a z1 + c z2 and z'2 = b z1 + d z2.
- Put tau = z2/z1 and z~ = -tau. Then -z'2/z'1 = -(d tau + b)/(c tau + a) = (d z~ - b)/(-c z~ + a).
- The coefficients are real, so conjugation commutes with this Möbius map. Hence z' = (d z - b)/(-c z + a) = g^{-1}·z in the usual Möbius sense.

To get a left action he then uses u -> u∘g^{-1}, with g^{-1} = (d -b; -c a). This gives (25 bis): z' = (a z + b)/(c z + d). He marks it 'victoire, c'est la formule habituelle'.

He immediately adds a caveat, continued on the next page. The usual formula holds only for his parameter z = -conj(z2/z1) in D. If one used tau = z2/z1 itself, which lies in the mirror image of D under reflection in the imaginary axis, the transformation formula would differ from the usual one.

This leads (p.138) to a theorem stated with that sign convention: D with the family E_z = C/(Z + Z(-conj z)) is a universal covering of M_{1,1}^{an}, classifying elliptic curves with Torelli rigidification. Its group of automorphisms over M_{1,1} is SL(2,Z), acting by the usual Möbius formula.
errors: Notational slip: in (25) the left-hand side is written z' = -z'2/z'1, omitting the complex conjugation required by (24) (z = -conj(z2/z1)). Strictly, the computed quantity is z~' = -z'2/z'1 = (d z~ - b)/(-c z~ + a). The final result is unaffected, because the Möbius coefficients are real and conjugation commutes with the map; the crossed-out line shows Grothendieck checking exactly this.
Otherwise the computation is correct. u -> u∘g induces z -> g^{-1}z, and u -> u∘g^{-1} induces z -> (az+b)/(cz+d).

ideas.what: Action of SL(2,Z) on framings (bases) of the period lattice of an elliptic curve, translated into the Möbius action on the half-plane parameter
ideas.modern_name: Modular group action on the upper half-plane / Teichmüller space of the torus; change of basis of the period lattice
ideas.where_published: Not in his published texts as such; the analytic construction of the modular family is in standard references (e.g. Deligne–Rapoport, Mumford, Hain's lectures).

ideas.what: Careful sign/conjugation convention: the point of D attached to a basis (z1,z2) is -conj(z2/z1), so that the induced action is the usual one; converting the right action u∘g into a left action via g^{-1}
ideas.modern_name: Left vs right action conventions; orientation conventions for period ratios

ideas.what: 'Structure de Torelli' as a rigidification of elliptic curves, with D as universal cover of M_{1,1}^{an}
ideas.modern_name: Framed (Teichmüller-marked) elliptic curves; the analytic moduli stack M_{1,1}^{an} = [H/SL(2,Z)]
ideas.usually_credited_to: Teichmüller theory; the stack-theoretic formulation is due to Deligne–Mumford and Deligne–Rapoport
ideas.where_published: The term 'structure de Torelli' is not standard; Esquisse d'un programme discusses Teichmüller towers but not this computation.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine, carefully executed verification of sign and action conventions, showing that the change of Torelli framing gives the standard Möbius formula. It has pedagogical and biographical interest, as Grothendieck redoes classical uniformization from scratch with attention to orientation and conjugation, but contains no new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'H ⊂ V' should most likely read 'Π ⊂ V' (or Π ⊂ t_E), consistent with the previous page ('π ⊂ ^tE') and with 'z'1, z'2 ∈ Π' two lines below.
'd'où une nouvelle formule [?]' appears in the image to read 'd'où immédiatement, pour z' = x'+iy' correspondant à u∘g^{-1}'.

'mod l [?]' is uncertain; the image shows a short word at the start of the line before 'on note que', perhaps 'mod 1' or 'via (24)'. It is not clearly 'mod l', and a level-l structure makes no sense here since the Torelli structures are full Z^2 framings.
The left-margin label is '(25)' with a struck-out earlier number; the marginal scribbles are cancellation checks for the sign manipulations in (25).
In (25) the last expression is (d z~ - b)/(-c z~ + a), where z~ denotes -z2/z1; the transcription renders this correctly, but the tilde marks z~ = -z2/z1 = conj(z).
